Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:33: In Ta'aniyot (7b) they said, rains are withheld only because of the brazen-faced, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:3), "and the showers have been withheld," etc., "and you had a harlot's forehead," etc. Rav Hamnuna said, whoever has a brazen face will eventually stumble into transgression, for it does not say "shall be" but "was" [suggesting habitual character rather than mere future event]. Rabbah bar Rav Huna said, it is permitted to call him wicked to his face. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said, it is permitted to hate him, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 8:1), "and the boldness of his face shall be changed [i.e., despised]." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:34: It is fitting to be careful of all the matters they said in Shabbat (32) — "because of such-and-such sin, this comes about" — and because of their length we have not quoted them, and shall quote only one of them, which is most commonly relevant: the sin causing the death of children. Rabbi says, because of the sin of [unfulfilled] vows, one's sons and daughters die while young, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth bring your flesh into guilt," etc., as we quoted in the Gate of Holiness (ch. 17); and this is also the view of Rabbi Elazar son of Rashbi (Shabbat, ibid.). There are those who say it is because of the sin of neglecting Torah study; some say because of neglecting the mezuzah; some say because of neglecting tzitzit — and all brought proof from verses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:35: Further there, it is taught: Rabbi Nechemiah says, because of the sin of baseless hatred, great strife arises within a person's household, and his wife miscarries, and his sons and daughters die while young. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:36: In Pesikta Rabbati (Yalkut, Jeremiah, siman 267, p. 60c) they said that the essential cause of children's death is the neglect of Torah, in these words: Rabbi Meir says, at the time Israel stood before Mount Sinai, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, bring Me guarantors that you will keep the Torah, and I will give it to you. They said to Him, our fathers are our guarantors. He said to them, I have claims against your fathers — Abraham, for saying (Genesis 15:8), "by what shall I know that I shall inherit it"; Isaac, for loving Esau; Jacob, for saying (Isaiah 40:27), "my way is hidden." They said to Him, our children are our guarantors. "Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings You have established strength" (Psalms 8:3) — and "strength" refers only to Torah, as it is said (Psalms 29:11), "the Lord will give strength to His people." At the time a borrower is seized and has nothing to repay, who is seized? Is it not the guarantor? Hence (Hosea 4:6), "and you have forgotten the Torah of your God, I will also forget your children" — so to speak, I too will suffer loss. Who said "bless" before Me? Was it not the children? Hence (Jeremiah 2:30), "in vain have I struck your children." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:37: Further they said in the Sifrei (parashat Ekev, siman 10): "and you shall teach them to your sons" — and not your daughters — the words of Rabbi Yosi ben Akiva. From here they said, when the child begins to speak, his father speaks with him in the Holy Tongue and teaches him Torah; if he does not speak with him in the Holy Tongue and teach him Torah, it is as though he buried him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 11:19), "and you shall teach them to your sons, that your days and your children's days be multiplied" — and if not, that your days and your children's days be shortened — for so words of Torah are expounded, from the affirmative you understand the negative. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:38: Regarding the merit of one who speaks in the Holy Tongue, it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Noach 74b) that the generation of the Dispersion succeeded in their deeds only because they spoke in the Holy Tongue, in these words: the secrets of Torah, the treasury of the Command, are spoken in the Holy Tongue, and the ministering angels recognize it, and would not speak in another tongue; therefore "and now nothing they propose will be withheld from them" (Genesis 11:6) — for had they spoken in another tongue, the supernal angels would not have recognized it, and their intention to do so would have been diminished. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:39: Further, one should be careful of the things of which it is said, "that which is crooked cannot be made straight" (Ecclesiastes 1:15) — explained in Bamidbar Rabbah (parashat Naso 9:6), in these words: "if his wife should go astray" — this is what is written (Proverbs 6:32), "whoever commits adultery with a woman lacks heart," etc.; "commits adultery with a woman" — this is what is written, "that which is crooked cannot be made straight," etc. It is taught: "that which is crooked cannot be made straight" — this refers to one who nullified the morning Shema or the evening Shema, or the morning prayer or the evening prayer; "and a deficiency cannot be counted" — this refers to one whose companions were counted for a matter of a commandment, and he was not counted among them. And there they brought this Mishnah, taught in Chagigah (1:7): Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says, what is "that which is crooked cannot be made straight"? This refers to one who engaged in forbidden relations and begot a mamzer from it — for should you say this refers to a thief or a robber, he can return and make it right. Further there in the Mishnah: Rashbi says, only one who was straight and became crooked is called "crooked" — and who is this? A Torah scholar who abandons Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:40: One should also be careful of what is explained in Midrash Rut from the Zohar (78a), that "a deficiency cannot be counted" refers to the three words missing from the Shema for the completion of 248 [words], and the prayer leader repeats and says, "the Lord your God is true," to complete the 248; and one who reads the Shema not with the congregation does not complete his 248 limbs, and of him it is said, "and a deficiency cannot be counted."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:41: A penitent who fasts every day must be careful that on the days he eats, such as Sabbaths, festivals, and Rosh Chodesh, he eat only fine foods, easy to digest, because a change in routine is the beginning of intestinal illness; and even from good things he should not fill his belly, lest he become ill and thereby nullify the morning or evening Shema, which is a positive commandment from the Torah. Likewise, public sanctification [kedushah], which is a commandment, as it is written, "and I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel," as explained in the Zohar, parashat Emor (93a). And likewise, he might stumble by having his companions counted for a matter of a commandment, praying in the synagogue with ten, while he is not counted among them — and one accustomed to coming to the synagogue, if for one day he does not come, the Holy One, blessed be He, asks after him (see Berachot 6b). Also he would not complete the 248 words of the Shema, which is "crooked and cannot be made straight." He would also nullify Torah study, which is a positive commandment from the Torah — and all this because of his own foolishness, as it is said (Proverbs 19:3), "the folly of man perverts his way," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:42: The wise man's eyes are in his head, and he should be a mighty man subduing his inclination, and not be drawn after his desire — especially on Rosh Chodesh and Purim, when the feast is by rabbinic ordinance, one must be careful not to fill his belly so that he becomes ill and thereby nullifies Torah study and prayer, which are positive commandments from the Torah — for a rabbinic positive commandment does not override a Torah positive commandment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:43: The rule is that a penitent must always be trembling and fearful of judgment, and must not forget how greatly he angered the Creator with his sins, and must fulfill, even on Sabbaths and festivals, "repent one day before your death" — for if he knew he would die on the Sabbath or a festival, how fearful and trembling he would be, and would rise early to read Torah, and would perform many good deeds, and would not be drawn after his pleasures. So he must do all his days, to rectify what he has perverted, on Sabbaths and festivals, and especially on days of joy, when a person is close to being drawn after his pleasures and his inclination will seduce him — great care is needed so that he not return to his former ways and become like a dog returning to its vomit, a fool repeating his folly, as has happened to many who returned to their former ways because of eating and drinking.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:44: Thus far our humble intellect has reached, in the brief words of our sages and the midrashim regarding repentance, and we did not wish to quote the words of the commentators so as not to elaborate further — but the penitent needs all of them, particularly the words of repentance of the Rokeach, which are matters received by tradition that the penitent must perform, and likewise regarding the repentance for one who has relations with a married woman, of which Sefer Chasidim speaks (siman 167), which the penitent must perform. Whoever wishes to perform complete repentance from heart and soul should not be negligent in seeking out the books needed for the healing of his soul, just as the sick person should not be negligent in seeking a physician to heal him — and my words in this Gate are only an exhortation to the penitent, and the things the early authors did not write, having left them as well known, are what I have written.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:45: In any case, we thought fit to quote the repentances written in Sefer HaMiddot (see Orchot Tzaddikim, Gate 26) found among us, whose words appear to be matters of tradition, in these words: and now one must write the matters of affliction for each and every transgression. One who has relations with a gentile woman shall fast three days and nights, three years, once a year; and if, Heaven forbid, after repentance he returns to his former way, he shall be stricter with himself even more, and in the summer season he shall go to a place with many ants and sit among them naked, and in the winter season he shall break the ice and sit in the water up to his nose; and if he still returns to his former way, he shall add even more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:46: One who emits seed in vain shall fast forty days, not necessarily consecutive, and shall sit in water in the winter season for the time it takes to roast an egg, and during those forty days shall not eat meat, nor anything warm at night, nor drink wine, except on Sabbaths and festivals, and shall wash his head lightly with water two or three times throughout those forty days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:47: One who has relations with his wife during her menstrual impurity shall fast forty consecutive days, and be lashed each day twice or three times, and shall not eat meat nor drink wine nor eat anything warm, except on Sabbaths and festivals, and shall not wash during all those days, and shall confess every day. And if he embraced or kissed his wife during her impurity, he shall fast forty days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:48: One who kisses or embraces other women shall fast Monday, Thursday, and Monday, and distance himself from her doorway. And if he had relations with an animal, a beast, or a bird, he shall fast forty days, and shall not wash, and shall not gaze at an animal, beast, or bird when they mate with one another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:49: A murderer shall go into exile for three years, and be lashed in every city, and say, I am a murderer, and shall not eat meat nor drink wine, nor shave the hair of his head or beard, nor launder his garments, nor wash his body — except that he shall wash his head once a month — and shall bind the hand with which he murdered, and his arm, with iron around his neck, and shall walk barefoot, and shall weep over his murder; and if someone insults him, he shall remain silent; and during those three years he shall not go on outings or engage in frivolity, and in his exile he shall lay himself before the entrance of the synagogue, and let all who pass by pass over him — but not tread upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:50: One who curses [his father/mother, or similar severe sin] shall remove his fine garments, and shall mourn and flee and afflict himself all the days of his life, and shall humble his spirit and his pride, and shall confess three times each day, and shall not eat meat or drink wine except on Sabbaths and festivals, and shall not wash, nor wash his head except once or twice a month, and shall not go to entertainment or weddings except for the seven blessings alone, and shall not sit among idol-worshipers even in a place where they speak words of Torah and commandments, and shall keep his distance from their entrances, and shall not benefit from them — and as soon as he repents he needs immersion, and shall bear affliction and suffering corresponding to his sins, for he denied the fundamental principle [of faith], and desecrated Sabbaths, and transgressed [sins liable to] excision and death by the court — therefore he needs great sufferings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:51: One who has relations with a married woman or a betrothed young woman — behold he forbids her to her husband once she has consented, and is liable to death by the court for her; therefore he shall bear affliction as harsh as death, and sit in snow and ice for one hour each day — thus he shall do throughout the winter each day, once or twice — and in the summer season he shall sit before flies or bees or other sufferings as harsh as death, and shall confess each day with weeping and sighing, and for a whole year shall not eat meat or drink wine except on Sabbath, festival, and Purim, and shall not eat warm bread, and shall not wash except lightly on the eves of festivals, and shall see no entertainment — though he may hear the blessings of bridegrooms — and shall not indulge himself in anything, and shall be lashed every day, and shall lie on the ground or on a single board without pillow or cushion — except that on Sabbath and festivals he shall lie on straw and hay with a pillow under his head — for he must break his coarse spirit from which his lust came, and his life shall be a life of affliction, and he shall wear sackcloth on his flesh, and shall not speak of matters of women's desire, and shall not gaze at women or their ornaments even when not worn, and shall not listen to the sound of music, and shall not speak with women at all, neither by hint nor by gesture nor in any manner, even with his own wife when she is menstrually impure, and shall not seclude himself with her in any seclusion.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:52: One who swears falsely, or violates a ban, must be lashed several times all his days, and confess for many days, and afterward be careful not to swear even truthfully, neither on the Torah nor on the souls of his ancestors, but rather he may vow by the life of his own head — but one may swear to fulfill a commandment. And he should be careful not to bring forth the Name of Heaven in vain from his mouth, and his limbs should tremble when he mentions the Name, and he should be careful of a blessing in vain, and if he unwittingly recited a blessing in vain, he should say afterward, "Blessed is the Name of the glory of His kingdom forever." And those who habituate themselves and their children to mention the Name of Heaven in the bathhouse or in a filthy place, to mention the Name of Heaven in vain — woe to them, woe to their children, for so they have taught their tongues; therefore he should guard and fence himself, his children, and his companions who listen to him, from mentioning the Name of Heaven in vain. And if this penitent needed to take an oath to his creditor, even a truthful one, he should fast that same day every year.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:53: If he was accustomed to speaking in the synagogue about any matter, even not during the time of prayer, he should sit with great awe and pray with intent, and fast forty days, whether consecutive or spread out, and be lashed with humility each day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:54: One who steals, or takes interest, should sit and ask forgiveness from him, and fast forty days or more, and confess each day, and be careful not to accept deposits, and not habitually go after his fellow's money, and perform acts of lovingkindness with his body and his money, and give from his own to those who labor in Torah and to those who fear Heaven. And if this one who took interest could avoid taking interest even from gentiles, it would be good.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:55: One who informs against his fellow, causing him to be hated in the eyes of the authority, and slanders him, and takes his money, and causes the death of his friend and his wife and children who depend on him — he shall repay his fellow all he lost, and ask his forgiveness, and be lashed and fast more than two years, and confess all the days of his life, for it is considered as though he killed his wife, his children, and his friend, and how many transgressions has he committed — therefore he shall break his spirit, and if he has nothing to repay, he shall increase his friends [to help repay] and ask his forgiveness, and be strict with himself, and repay him or his heirs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:56: A talebearer and the like — there is no remedy until he asks forgiveness from him, and he shall be lashed and fast forty days or more and be lashed each day, and all his affairs shall be in commandments and in the pursuit of peace between every person and between every man and his wife.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:57: One who strikes his fellow or distresses him, whether financially or through verbal fraud, has no atonement unless he appeases his fellow, and Yom Kippur atones only for transgressions between him and the Omnipresent, but transgressions between him and his fellow require that he appease him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:58: One who raises his hand against his fellow is called wicked, and shall ask his forgiveness and be atoned. One who shames his fellow's face shall fast forty days or more and be lashed each day and confess all the days of his life. One who gives his fellow a nickname shall ask his forgiveness publicly, and be lashed and fast forty days, and confess each day with humility.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:59: One who wrongs a convert shall ask his forgiveness, and be lashed and fast each day. One who provokes his fellow shall bring three rows of people, and say, I have sinned, I have committed iniquity, and it does not equal for me, and ask his forgiveness three times and no more; and if he has died, he shall bring ten people to his grave and say, I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel and against so-and-so whom I provoked — this applies specifically when he did not disgrace him publicly and appeasement did not suffice from the start, and the one being asked for forgiveness should not be cruel [in refusing]. And if he provoked him and gave him a bad name, there is no forgiveness for him ever unless he fasts and is lashed privately for forty days or more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:60: One who desecrates the Name — desecration of the Name is a great sin — and what is desecration of the Name? Rav said, such as myself, who goes to the butcher and takes meat and does not pay the money immediately — meaning, he brings himself to be lightly regarded regarding theft, and people learn from him and become more lenient because of him. Rabbi Yochanan said, such as myself, who walks four cubits without tefillin and without Torah, and people learn more from him. Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel, it is better for a person to transgress a sin in private than to desecrate the Name of Heaven publicly — meaning, so that people do not learn from his deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:61: Rabbi Ila'i the Elder said, if a person sees that his inclination overpowers him, let him go to a place where he is not known, and dress in black, and do what his heart desires, but let him not desecrate the Name of Heaven publicly. And the sages explained — Heaven forbid that they permitted him to transgress a sin — but the sages say that he should stand against his evil inclination, since he only desires, for all that is forbidden to him, to fulfill his desire; and since he goes into exile far away and dresses in black, he will then break and humble himself and restrain his heart from sin — but to commit a forbidden act, not at all, at all — rather, these deeds break the evil inclination and restrain it from transgressing, as Rabbi Ila'i said, for the fatigue of travel, wearing black, and being a stranger break the evil inclination and restrain it from transgression.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:62: And it is said, whoever does not have regard for his Creator's honor, it would have been fitting for him not to have come into the world; and we say in the Gemara, Rav Yosef said, this is one who transgresses a sin in private, in the manner of Rabbi Yitzchak, for Rabbi Yitzchak said, whoever transgresses a sin in private is as though he pushes against the feet of the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:63: Desecration of the Name is a sin that has fruits — when one does an evil thing, others learn from him. Of this sin, everyone must be very afraid, for desecration of the Name occurs in many ways without limit — for whoever demeans even one commandment and treats the honor of Heaven lightly is called a desecrator of the Name, for others learn from him and become more lenient and treat it lightly.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:64: If a person transgressed [sins liable to] excision or death by the court, repentance and Yom Kippur atone for half, and sufferings atone for half; but if desecration of the Name of Heaven occurred through him, repentance has no power to suspend, nor Yom Kippur to atone, nor sufferings to scour, but rather all of these together suspend, and death alone scours away the sin. Therefore a person should be careful of desecration of the Name and distance himself from ugliness and from that which resembles it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:65: The essential repentance for desecration of the Name is that he make known his sins before the multitude, and say to them, do not learn from me, for I have sinned, I have committed iniquity, I have transgressed, I have desecrated the Name through my folly — and he shall fast several fasts, and confess every day until his day of death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:66: For every single transgression a person commits, whether unwittingly or intentionally — such as touching a Sabbath candle, or lighting a candle on Sabbath, not remembering it is Sabbath, or acting unknowingly — he must confess and fast at least two days, Monday and Thursday. And so he should do for all the great transgressions a person commits — he should fast — and there are two benefits in this: first, that the fast atones; second, that it prevents transgressions, for he will think in his heart, if I do this I must fast, and thereby refrain from the transgression.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:67: This is the great fence before all transgressions — that he penalize himself, or give charity, or cause distress to his body when he has transgressed a sin — and he should do this for all the transgressions he is accustomed to, such as jealousy, hatred, [excessive] joy, idle words, and slander, or that he did not have proper intent in blessings and prayer, uttering blessings from his mouth without intent, and many other similar matters. Therefore he should examine himself each day regarding these matters, and if he encountered one of these and transgressed it, he should hasten to be distressed over them and confess whatever sin he committed, seeking forgiveness from the Name with a broken heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:68: A great matter is confession, for our sages taught: when he was about ten cubits from the place of stoning, they would say to him, confess — for such is the way of the condemned, to confess, since whoever confesses has a portion in the World to Come; and if he does not know how to confess, he should say, may it be Your will that my death be an atonement for all my sins — for so we find regarding Achan, that Joshua said to him (Joshua 7:19), "my son, give glory now to the Lord, and give confession to Him," and Achan answered and said, "indeed, I have sinned."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:69: For every commandment, whether positive or negative, if one transgressed one of them, whether intentionally or unwittingly, when he repents of his sins he is obligated to confess before God, exalted be He, as it is said (Numbers 5:7), "a man or a woman who commits any of the sins that men commit," etc., "shall confess their sin which they have done" — and this is verbal confession. All who are liable to sin-offerings and guilt-offerings, and all liable to death by the court and lashes, are not atoned by their death, their lashes, or their sacrifice until they perform repentance and confess. And whoever damages or causes monetary loss to his fellow, even though he repays him, is not atoned until he confesses and returns from ever doing such a thing again.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:70: How does he confess? He says, please, O Name, I have sinned, I have committed iniquity, I have transgressed before You, thus and thus I have done, and behold I regret and am ashamed of my deeds, and I shall never return to this matter — and this is the essence of confession, that he not return to his former ways. Whoever increases confession and elaborates on this matter is praiseworthy. Also this is essential to confession — that he say, "but we have sinned." And it is very good to specify the sin within the confession — such as, if he ate carrion or non-kosher meat or other forbidden things, he should specify this within his confession. How? When he says "I have been guilty," he should say, I ate something impure. When he says "I have betrayed," if he had relations with a gentile woman or a married woman or a menstrually impure woman, he should say, I had relations. If he stole or robbed, he should say, I robbed. If he gave his fellow a bad name, or slandered him, or excommunicated him wrongly, he should say, I spoke slander of him. If he emitted seed in vain, he should say, I committed iniquity. If he committed adultery with forbidden relations, he should say, I acted presumptuously, I committed harlotry. If he desecrated the Sabbath or coveted, he should say, I desecrated, I coveted — and so for each letter of the alphabet.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:71: And afterward he should specify in the confession the transgression he committed, and say, with weeping, "let the wicked forsake his way, and the man of iniquity his thoughts" — and then it will avail him. The end of the confession: "I have turned away from Your good commandments and Your judgments, and it did not profit me; and You are righteous concerning all that has come upon me, for You have acted truly and I have acted wickedly." And then he shall say, thus have I transgressed positive and negative commandments, and I have transgressed [sins liable to] excision and death at the hand of Heaven, I have transgressed those liable to death by the court, and the Written Torah and the Oral Torah, I have forgotten Your great Name, I have forgotten the yoke of Your kingship and Your fear, and You are righteous concerning all, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:72: In the Yerushalmi (Yoma, ch. 8, halachah 9) it is explained how to confess: he says, Master of the worlds, I have done evil in Your eyes, and I have walked in the willfulness of my heart, and I have not heeded Your rebuke; may it be Your will, O Lord my God and God of my fathers, that You atone for me for all my transgressions, and forgive me for all my iniquities, and pardon me for all my sins, etc. — end of quotation.
